registry_title: Global Central Bank Rate-Path & Macro Projection Registry
usage_note: Extends the 'official' tier of forecast_sources_registry.json (which only covered the Fed) to every major economy. Use this to source the rate-path and GDP/inflation assumption for any non-US revenue segment in the macro_to_company_pipeline.md Step 4 derivation -- e.g. a Europe segment now points to 'ecb_projections' instead of being flagged as a gap.
critical_distinction: Not all central banks publish a rate path the way the Fed's SEP dot plot does. This matters a lot for how confidently you can use their number as a discount-rate input. Three categories, tagged per entry as 'rate_path_transparency': (1) EXPLICIT_OWN_PATH -- the bank publishes its own multi-year policy rate forecast (rare, and the strongest signal when available); (2) MARKET_CONDITIONED -- the bank publishes GDP/inflation forecasts conditioned on the market's forward rate curve, not its own view of where rates are going (most common among G10); (3) OPAQUE_OR_POLITICAL -- limited/no formal forward guidance, forecasts are more descriptive than predictive (notably PBoC).

central_banks.publication: ECB (Mar/Sep) and Eurosystem (Jun/Dec) staff macroeconomic projections
central_banks.methodology: Staff projections conditioned on market-implied interest rate expectations, not a Governing Council-published path; Governing Council decisions and guidance are communicated separately in the post-meeting statement.

access.endpoint_or_series_id: ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (SDW) SDMX 2.1 REST API, base https://sdw-wsrest.ecb.europa.eu; Python (sdw-api) and R (ecb) packages available

central_banks.automation_feasibility: high -- genuine free REST/SDMX API, no registration required
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for any Euro-area revenue segment; also has its own ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters (quarterly) as a secondary consensus cross-check.

central_banks.methodology: Baseline projection explicitly conditioned on the market-implied Bank Rate path, derived from a 15-working-day average of forward market rates ahead of each report -- the MPC does not publish its own rate-path forecast.

access.endpoint_or_series_id: Bank of England IADB (Interactive Database), CSV/XML/HTML export via URL parameters (up to 300 series codes per request); R package 'boe' available

central_banks.automation_feasibility: high -- free database API, no auth
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for UK revenue segments. Because the forecast is explicitly conditioned on market rates rather than the MPC's own view, treat the 'market curve implied path' quoted in each report as the actual rate-path input, not the GDP/CPI numbers alone.

central_banks.publication: Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices (Outlook Report)
central_banks.methodology: Median of individual Policy Board members' point-estimate forecasts (highest and lowest excluded), published as a range. No explicit policy-rate path is published; forward guidance is qualitative.

access.endpoint_or_series_id: BOJ Time-Series Data Search API, JSON/CSV output, official API service; Python (bojpy) and R (BOJ) wrappers exist

central_banks.automation_feasibility: high -- genuine official free API with documented manual
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for Japan revenue segments. Given no published rate path, pair this with money-market futures (OIS) for the actual rate assumption rather than inferring one from the Outlook Report.

forecasts: Descriptive GDP growth commentary (tracks the NPC's political 'around X%' annual growth target rather than an independent forecast)
central_banks.methodology: Limited institutional independence relative to Western central banks (reports to the State Council); forward guidance is restricted and the 'target' is better read as a political growth objective than a statistical forecast.

access.method: web publication, no structured API found

central_banks.automation_feasibility: low -- no API; treat as a manually-reviewed input
central_banks.pipeline_role: For any China revenue exposure, weight the IMF WEO / OECD China projections (already in forecast_sources_registry.json) more heavily than PBoC's own report, and treat the NPC's annual growth target as a policy anchor rather than a forecast.

central_banks.methodology: Base-case projection for growth and inflation plus explicit risk assessment; does not publish its own policy-rate path.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- structured projections tables published per report but no dedicated REST API found; scrape the projections page each cycle
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for Canada revenue segments; note current reports flag US trade-relationship risk explicitly, relevant for any cross-border NA segment already covered by the Fed-side entries.

central_banks.methodology: Forecast tables with historical archive; explicitly discusses risks to the outlook alongside the base case.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium-high -- forecast archive tables are downloadable, structured, and versioned
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for Australia/APAC-adjacent revenue segments (mining/commodity-linked exposure especially).

central_banks.publication: Monetary Policy Statement (MPS) — OCR projection track
central_banks.methodology: One of the few central banks that publishes its own explicit multi-year OCR projection track, not merely a market-conditioned assumption -- directly analogous to the Fed's SEP dot plot.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- data available but check for a structured export vs. PDF-only release
central_banks.pipeline_role: Small direct portfolio weight for most books, but useful as a rare 'ground truth' explicit rate path when validating whether market-conditioned approaches (BoE-style) are over/under-shooting elsewhere.

central_banks.publication: Monetary Policy Report (MPR) — policy rate path + fan chart
central_banks.methodology: Publishes its own explicit policy-rate path (not market-conditioned) plus a fan chart showing forecast-error-based uncertainty bands that widen further out the horizon.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- structured web reports, verify export options
central_banks.pipeline_role: Same 'ground truth' role as RBNZ -- useful reference for validating rate-path methodology elsewhere, plus directly relevant for any Norway/Nordic energy-linked revenue exposure.

central_banks.publication: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) resolution + bi-monthly policy statements
central_banks.cadence: bi-monthly policy decisions (6x/year), forecasts revised at each
central_banks.methodology: Repo rate decided by MPC vote; GDP/CPI projections revised at every bi-monthly meeting rather than a fixed quarterly cycle, so forecasts can move more frequently than G10 peers.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- no dedicated forecast API found, requires monitoring press releases/PIB announcements each cycle
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for India revenue exposure; note the CPI target band is explicit (2-6%, 4% midpoint), useful as a standing reference point for inflation-surprise magnitude.

central_banks.publication: Focus Survey (Boletim Focus) + quarterly Inflation Report
central_banks.cadence: Focus survey: weekly; Inflation Report: quarterly
central_banks.methodology: Focus is a survey of ~100 market economists (functionally Brazil's SPF/Blue Chip equivalent), published weekly -- unusually high-frequency for a consensus survey, letting it react fast to data surprises.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: high -- BCB publishes structured expectations-system data, well-documented in BCB working papers
central_banks.pipeline_role: Best-in-class EM consensus instrument in this registry given its weekly cadence -- useful template if you want the same frequency for other EM exposure.

central_banks.publication: Quarterly Report + Citibanamex (Citi Mexico) Expectations Survey
central_banks.cadence: Quarterly Report: quarterly; Citibanamex survey: bi-weekly/fortnightly
central_banks.methodology: Banxico's own Quarterly Report gives GDP/inflation ranges; the Citibanamex survey is a private bank-run consensus poll (~30 banks) functioning as a faster-moving cross-check, similar in spirit to Brazil's Focus survey.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- PDF-based reports, no dedicated forecast API found
central_banks.pipeline_role: Primary driver for Mexico/nearshoring-exposed revenue segments.

central_banks.publication: Monetary Policy Assessment — conditional inflation forecast
central_banks.methodology: Distinctive approach: the inflation forecast is explicitly conditioned on an assumption of an UNCHANGED policy rate over the full 3-year horizon. Because of this fixed assumption, changes in the forecast itself (not a stated path) are what signal the SNB's likely future direction -- a rising forecast implies future tightening bias, a falling one implies easing bias.
central_banks.automation_feasibility: medium -- structured quarterly releases, verify export format
central_banks.pipeline_role: Useful for Swiss-franc-denominated revenue/financing exposure; the 'unchanged rate' framing means you read the *forecast drift* as the signal, not a stated path -- flag this methodology difference clearly if feeding it into the same schema field as Norway/NZ's explicit paths.

coverage_gaps_worth_flagging: No South Korea (Bank of Korea), no broader Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand) central banks covered yet -- add if any holding has meaningful exposure there.

No Sweden (Riksbank) or Czech National Bank -- both also publish EXPLICIT_OWN_PATH rate forecasts like Norway/NZ and would be good additions to the 'ground truth' comparison set if European exposure grows.
PBoC entry is the weakest in this registry by design -- China's opacity is a real analytical constraint, not a research gap to be solved; lean on IMF/OECD/private-bank China desks instead.
